the average annual emissions of industrial air pollutants are higher for the 20% poorest census tracts than for the 20 richest census tracts in the United States, that the emissions of industrial air toxics are also higher in census tracts with higher proportions of minorities, and that these differences in emissions are statistically significant at a high confidence level.

the average annual industrial emissions of air toxics per person in 2002 in census tracts with a majority of non-Hispanic black or Hispanic people was 1.3 and 1.2 times, respectively, the average for all census tracts.
